name: Nepal
genZNote: Home to 8 of the world's 10 highest peaks and an open border with India — Nepal really said 'mountains AND easy travel', pick both.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A landlocked Himalayan country between India (south, east, west) and China/Tibet (north).
Home to Mount Everest (Sagarmatha), the world's highest peak, on the border with Tibet, plus 7 other of the world's 10 highest mountains.
Terrain ranges from the Terai plains in the south to the high Himalayas in the north.
Capital: Kathmandu, in the Kathmandu Valley.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Nepali is the official language; the country is religiously and culturally diverse, with a Hindu-majority population and a significant Buddhist heritage.
Lumbini, in southern Nepal, is the birthplace of Gautama Buddha and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Kathmandu Valley itself holds multiple UNESCO-listed monument zones (temples, stupas, palace squares).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal democratic republic since 2008, when the 240-year-old Shah monarchy was abolished following a Constituent Assembly vote.
The current Constitution was promulgated in 2015, establishing Nepal as a secular, federal republic with 7 provinces.
Head of state: President; head of government: Prime Minister; unicameral Federal Parliament's lower house is the House of Representatives.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Member of the United Nations and SAARC (headquartered relationships across South Asia).
Maintains close ties with both India and China, its only two neighbours, balancing relations with each.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Nepal share an open border allowing free movement of citizens, a distinctive feature of the relationship.
The 1950 Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship underpins close diplomatic, security, and economic ties.
India is one of Nepal's largest trading partners and a major source of hydropower cooperation and infrastructure investment.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Tourism (mountaineering, trekking, pilgrimage) is a major economic pillar, alongside agriculture and remittances from Nepali workers abroad.
Significant hydropower potential from its mountain rivers, with growing hydroelectric cooperation with India.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Mount Everest and Himalayan mountaineering/trekking tourism.
Lumbini (Buddha's birthplace) and the Kathmandu Valley's temple architecture.
An open border and treaty-based close relationship with India.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Nepalese Rupee (NPR), pegged to the Indian Rupee.
Tourism (especially mountaineering) and agriculture are central to the economy; remittances from workers abroad form a large share of national income.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, and eight of the world's fourteen 8,000-metre mountains.
Chitwan National Park protects significant populations of the one-horned rhinoceros and Bengal tiger.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Unified as a single kingdom in the 18th century by Prithvi Narayan Shah.
Never colonized by a foreign power; ended a decade-long Maoist insurgency in 2006, leading to the abolition of the monarchy in 2008.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 2008 abolition of the 240-year-old monarchy established Nepal as a federal democratic republic.
The 2015 Constitution formalized federalism, dividing the country into seven provinces.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Mountaineering and trekking define its global reputation, centred on the Himalayas and Everest.
Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha, is a UNESCO World Heritage pilgrimage site.
Kathmandu Valley's ancient temple squares are also UNESCO-listed.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of SAARC; member of the UN.
A significant contributor of Gurkha soldiers to international military forces historically and troops to UN peacekeeping missions.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Nepal is a landlocked Himalayan federal democratic republic between India and China, home to Mount Everest and Lumbini.
keyFacts: Became a federal democratic republic in 2008; current Constitution promulgated in 2015 (7 provinces).
Lumbini is the birthplace of Gautama Buddha.
Open border with India, governed by the 1950 Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship.
commonConfusion: Everest sits on the Nepal-Tibet (China) border, not entirely within one country — both share the peak.

highYieldFacts: Nepal became a republic in 2008, ending the Shah monarchy; its current Constitution dates to 2015.
The India-Nepal open border is a distinctive, frequently tested feature of the relationship.
commonTraps: Assuming Nepal is still a monarchy — it became a federal republic in 2008.
mustRemember: Lumbini = Buddha's birthplace, in Nepal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
